draft.title: Predicting from trends
card: A trend is a pattern of change over time in economic data, such as prices or interest rates rising for several months.
To make a prediction, find the likely cause of the trend. Then ask what effect it will have and who is affected.

Example: if interest rates rise, loans cost more. Households with variable rate loans pay more, so they have less to spend on housing. Demand for homes is likely to ease, so house prices are likely to slow.
A prediction says what is likely, not certain. Other things, such as a change in income, can change the outcome.
draft.remember: Spot the trend, find its cause, then predict who is affected and how.

a.q: Interest rates have risen for several months and a bank passes this on. What is the likely effect on a household with a variable rate home loan?
opts: Their loan repayments become larger
Their loan repayments become smaller
Their loan repayments stay the same
Their loan is paid off sooner
a.why: A higher rate means the family pays more interest, so repayments are likely to rise. Smaller repayments would follow a fall in rates, which is the opposite trend.
a.clue: Think about what a higher rate means for the cost of borrowing.

b.q: Petrol prices in Melbourne have climbed for six months because oil costs more. What is the most likely effect on a person who drives far to work each day?
opts: Less money left over for other spending
More money left over for other spending
No change in what they spend on petrol
A lower cost of getting to work
b.why: The trend is rising petrol prices, so a long commute now costs more. With more spent on petrol, less is left for other things. Falling costs would need the trend to run the other way.
b.clue: Link the rising price to the driver's weekly costs.

b.best: Less money left over for other spending

problems.detail: The example's chain is muddled. Households already paying more on variable rate loans having 'less to spend on housing' is not why demand for homes eases. The main link is that higher rates make new loans dearer, so buyers can borrow less. Also, 'house prices are likely to slow' should say price growth is likely to slow.

It also says 'prices slow' where it means price growth slows.

opts: House price growth slows as buyers can borrow less
House price growth speeds up as loans cost more
Demand for homes rises as buyers can borrow more

a.clue: Follow the chain from the cost of a loan to how much buyers can borrow.
